tema: if decides; else is plan B; === compares.

charla.texto: Lesson three: conditionals. if asks something. If it's true, it does one thing; if not, else does another.
To compare you use three equals signs: ===. A single one, =, doesn't compare: it assigns. It's the most common mistake in the world.
jair lives in the else. the if hasn't come true in eight years
if (Rikka kisses me) { I win the dare } else { …I like it too }. Did I say that out loud?
You said it out loud, Cami! In front of the instructor!
Don't be like that. I spanked you at the hot springs and you didn't even complain.
Because I was in shock! A five-hundred-year-old heroine doesn't know what to do with that.
…Exercise. A function that decides what to do based on Nikki's message. Please. Focus.

=    assigns (stores). It does NOT compare. Don't mix them up.
decaf = nothing. An empty value (in JavaScript, null).
Written at 1:31 a.m., waiting for a message.

1.error: “{valor}” doesn't compare. To ask whether two things are equal you use ===.

2.error: “{valor}” isn't plan B. After an if, what happens when it isn't true goes in else.

3.error: “{valor}” isn't “nothing”. In Coffee, the empty value is decaf.

exito: ✔ Compiled. Finally an if that comes true in the instructor's life.

al_abrir.texto: Watch out for = and ===. One stores, the other asks. It's the most expensive mistake in history.
